narr: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania with moderate CAPE and very little CIN ahead of an approaching cold front. A few of the storms produced sporadic wind damage, and the widespread nature of this activity allowed the event to evolve into a flash flooding threat as well.
ev: Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches led to the closure of Brush Valley Road between Schock and Tressler roads in Rockefeller Township due to flash flooding.
Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches led to the closure of Route 61 between Highland Avenue in Sunbury and Green Street in Upper Augusta Township due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain led to the washout of a roadway between Tuscarora Township and Mifflintown.
Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches caused flash flooding east of Sunbury, with emergency responders conducting a water rescue on Plum Creek Road.

Heavy rainfall led to flash flooding of roads, a park, and a residential area in Thompsontown. There was also damage to the local fire station that included the kitchen, restroom, a meeting room, and a truck bay.
